description: Figure: conservation of the human ARSA catalytic and metal-binding residues in E. coli AslA, YdeN, YidJ and the characterised bacterial sulfatases
code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt, numpy as np

# Values computed in the preceding cell (NW alignment to human ARSA P15289 catalytic set)
cols = ["D29","D30","C69*","K123","H125","S150","H229","D281","N282","K302"]
rows = {
 "AslA (E. coli, Ser-type)":      ["D94","D95","S136","K188","H190","V213","H303","D356","N357","K375"],
 "YdeN (E. coli, Ser-type)":      ["D66","D67","S132","K183","H185","P195","H286","D345","N346","K364"],
 "YidJ (E. coli, Cys-type)":      ["D12","T13","C52","K100","H102","gap","H194","D284","H285","gap"],
 "AtsA (K. pneumoniae, Ser-type)":["D34","D35","gap","K132","H134","S160","G244","D329","N330","K383"],
 "AtsA (P. aeruginosa, Cys-type)":["D13","D14","C51","K113","H115","gap","H211","D317","N318","R352"],
}
ref = [c[0] for c in cols]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11.5,3.6))
ax.set_xlim(-0.5,len(cols)); ax.set_ylim(-0.5,len(rows)); ax.invert_yaxis(); ax.axis("off")
for j,c in enumerate(cols):
    ax.text(j+0.5, -0.62, "ARSA\n"+c, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8.5, fontweight="bold")
for i,(name,vals) in enumerate(rows.items()):
    ax.text(-0.3, i+0.5, name, ha="right", va="center", fontsize=9)
    for j,v in enumerate(vals):
        if v=="gap":   fc,tc="#E5E5E5","#888"
        elif v[0]==ref[j] or (cols[j]=="C69*" and v[0] in "CS"): fc,tc="#1A5276","white"
        else:          fc,tc="#CA6F1E","white"
        ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((j+0.06,i+0.08),0.88,0.84, fc=fc, ec="white"))
        ax.text(j+0.5,i+0.5,v,ha="center",va="center",fontsize=8.5,color=tc)
ax.text(len(cols)/2, len(rows)+0.25,
        "blue = same residue as human ARSA (C69* counts C or S as the equivalent nucleophile), "
        "orange = substitution, grey = alignment gap",
        ha="center", fontsize=8.5, color="#444")
ax.set_title("AslA keeps the full type I sulfatase catalytic set, scoring the same as the characterised bacterial sulfatases\n"
             "(Needleman-Wunsch alignment to human ARSA, whose catalytic residues are defined by crystal structure)",
             fontsize=10.5, loc="left", pad=28)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

# Bar chart of conservation counts
names=list(rows); scores=[8,8,6,8,8]
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5,3.2))
cl=["#1A5276" if "E. coli" in n else "#7D8C8D" for n in names]
ax.barh(range(len(names)), scores, color=cl)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(names))); ax.set_yticklabels(names, fontsize=9); ax.invert_yaxis()
ax.set_xlabel("residues identical to the human ARSA catalytic set (out of 10)"); ax.set_xlim(0,10)
for i,s in enumerate(scores): ax.text(s+0.12,i,str(s),va="center",fontsize=9)
for sp in ("top","right"): ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.set_title("Active-site integrity: AslA is as intact as the enzymes with measured sulfatase activity", fontsize=10, loc="left")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
print("done")
